title: Meals together
hookLine: at Emmaus, two travelers knew him in the breaking of bread: grace, and no screens
tomorrow: a new monk asked to be taught. why was he told to wash his bowl?

lines: A STRANGER ON THE ROAD TO EMMAUS.
cards: Two phones face-up on the table, both lighting up. Luke's Gospel tells of a supper with a stranger at it. Two followers of Jesus are walking to a village called Emmaus, talking over his death.
A traveler falls in beside them, asks what they're discussing, and walks with them all the way, opening the scriptures. At the village they press him to stay.
Then: "as he sat at meat with them, he took bread, and blessed it, and brake, and gave to them. And their eyes were opened, and they knew him".

teach.b: Not on the road. Luke says their eyes were held there, so they wouldn't know him: the whole walk, they talked with him and didn't see who he was. They knew him at the table, at the blessing and the broken bread.
They hurry back to Jerusalem that same hour and tell the others how he was known of them in breaking of bread. Christians read this meal in different ways.

teach.h: HE TOOK BREAD, AND BLESSED IT.
teach.b: Catholics and Orthodox Christians hear the Eucharist in it: bread taken, blessed, broken and given at every Mass and liturgy. Other Christians hear the Lord's Supper, or every table where grace is said.
Grace before a meal keeps that order: thanks first, then the bread, as he did it at the table where their eyes opened.
Here's where it meets a weeknight.
A meal can be a place you finally see the person across from you, if the table is clear enough to see them.

how: Christians say grace before meals, giving thanks over bread, and churches share bread taken, blessed, broken and given at the Eucharist or the Lord's Supper.

o: sharing a table with your attention on the people there
eating the same food at the same time as everyone
a holiday feast with the whole extended family

games.q: the supper at Emmaus: tap the pairs.
p: the village the two were walking to
opened the scriptures on the road

s: the two knew Jesus as soon as he joined them on the road
they walked with him all the way and knew him only at the table.
Luke says he was known of them in breaking of bread
that's how they told it to the others back in Jerusalem.

games.q: your aunt says grace before family dinner, and your cousin rolls his eyes. what does Emmaus say happened at a blessing?
o: eyes opened: they knew him when he blessed and broke the bread.
nothing new; in the story everything important happened on the road.
the blessing was a polite custom the travelers taught their guest.
games.why: he took bread, blessed it, broke it, gave it, and their eyes were opened.

practice: Bring to mind your next meal and who will be at it, or who you'd want there. Count three things on that table you didn't make yourself: the bread, the hands that grew it, the face across from you.
Rest with the count until the bell.

wordCard.voice: Meals together: a table where the thanks come first and the faces aren't behind screens. At Emmaus, they knew him there.

orig.note: Greek: the breaking of the bread, Luke's phrase for how they knew him.

carryVoice: Your line: together. The two at Emmaus walked the whole road, and saw him at the table. One week, gathered.
